preparation11.title: Prep for Splunk 11.x
preparation11.scope: Upcoming Splunk Enterprise 11.x and later major releases
preparation11.summary: Follow public announcements, understand the decisions ahead, and prepare against documented current capabilities while 11.x details develop.
preparation11.boundary: No version-specific public 11.x release announcement was located in the sources checked on October 15, 2026. Release timing, deployment requirements and migration paths remain unconfirmed here.
preparation11.announcementPolicy: An announcement records a stated plan. Released documentation, exact compatibility matrices and service-specific evidence are required before a plan becomes an installation path, supported pairing or availability claim.

baseline.title: Start with an exact Operator compatibility tuple
baseline.text: The 3.2 help matrix lists Kubernetes 1.32–1.37 and Enterprise 9.4.15–10.6.0. The linked change log lists Kubernetes 1.32–1.36 and Enterprise 10.6.0 for 3.2.0. Its September 8 heading also differs from the matrix’s September 24 release date.
baseline.qualification: Preserve both published scopes. Confirm the exact Kubernetes, Operator and Enterprise combination before using it; neither source certifies 11.x.
baseline.action: Record the intended Kubernetes distribution and version, Operator release and exact Enterprise build. Resolve the differing 3.2 version/date statements before relying on their disputed range.

baseline.title: Design storage and failure recovery before moving workloads
baseline.text: The Operator validated architecture describes single-site and multi-site layouts, persistent storage, SmartStore and the App Framework. It discourages distributed non-clustered deployments because they lack the redundancy expected in Kubernetes.
baseline.qualification: Current architecture guidance is preparation context. An 11.x topology, sizing or migration requirement is not established.
baseline.action: Map search heads, indexers and management roles to availability zones, storage classes, recovery objectives and a tested restore design.

baseline.title: Inventory apps and configuration delivery
baseline.version: Current Operator App Framework and premium-app guidance
baseline.text: The current Operator architecture covers app distribution through the App Framework and separate considerations for premium apps. Existing apps, add-ons, scripts, credentials and filesystem assumptions need their own review.
baseline.qualification: App installation and a container image do not prove ES, ITSI, SOAR or third-party compatibility with 11.x.
baseline.action: Build an app and integration inventory, identify persistent state and external dependencies, and plan repeatable deployment and rollback tests. Keep exact premium-product matrices as a separate decision gate.

baseline.title: Recheck search resource controls
baseline.text: Current workload-management guidance distinguishes Advanced mode, requiring writable CPU and memory cgroups, from Basic mode, which supports admission rules on systems such as Kubernetes.
baseline.qualification: Basic mode does not establish full workload-pool or placement-rule parity. This is current-release behavior, not an 11.x promise.
baseline.action: Inventory admission, placement and monitoring rules; validate which controls work in the chosen current lab topology before assuming equivalent behavior.

baseline.title: Compare the future operating model with a Cloud migration
baseline.version: Current Splunk Cloud Platform migration guidance
baseline.text: Splunk Lantern’s migration readiness guidance calls for team ownership, communication and an operating model for the move to Splunk Cloud Platform.
baseline.qualification: Cloud is a separate migration program. Enterprise announcements do not establish Cloud rollout, entitlement or FedRAMP Moderate/High authorization.
baseline.action: Assess ownership, staffing, communication and post-migration responsibilities. Use the released Enterprise-to-Cloud guide for technical assessment and exact service-specific evidence.

questions.title: When will 11.x be available, and at what release stage?
questions.text: A confirmed public release date, preview or general-availability stage is not recorded in this evidence set.
questions.needed: A dated official announcement and version-specific release notes.

questions.title: What deployment models will 11.x support?
questions.text: Supported deployment models, platform requirements and component-specific support for 11.x remain unconfirmed here.
questions.needed: Version-specific system requirements and an official deployment/support statement.

questions.title: How will existing deployments reach 11.x?
questions.text: No 10.x-to-11.x upgrade edge, in-place conversion or data-movement procedure is published in this guide.
questions.needed: READ THIS FIRST, an exact upgrade-path table, migration procedure and rollback limits.

questions.title: Which premium products, apps and forwarders will pair?
questions.text: Existing 10.x support does not establish 11.x support for ES, ITSI, SOAR, apps, forwarders or receiver topologies.
questions.needed: Exact app, runtime, premium-product and forwarder/receiver matrices.

questions.title: What changes for support, security and lifecycle?
questions.text: No 11.x support deadline, runtime floor, FIPS status or security baseline is inferred from adjacent releases.
questions.needed: The applicable public support-policy line, system requirements, advisories and cryptographic guidance.

questions.title: What changes for Cloud or regulated environments?
questions.text: Commercial Enterprise plans do not establish a Cloud service date, regional rollout or FR-M/FR-H authorization.
questions.needed: Current Cloud Service Details, product-specific regional evidence and exact authorized Marketplace offerings.

monitoring.scope: Discover official public 11.x+ announcements and version-specific documentation; recheck this finite source inventory and affected claims; coordinate ES editions and Cloud/FedRAMP evidence with their existing owners.
monitoring.outcome: No version-specific 11.x announcement located; current preparation context verified
monitoring.followUp: Add the first verifiable public 11.x announcement with its exact statement, source date, release stage, applicability and remaining unknowns. Preserve prior statements as dated history.

contextUpdates.title: Review custom version-detection logic
contextUpdates.text: The 10.6 announcement asks app and automation owners to use supported product-identification methods rather than relying on version numbers alone to distinguish Enterprise from Cloud.
contextUpdates.qualification: This is published 10.6 guidance and a useful preparation task. It does not announce an 11.x release or a migration path.

contextUpdates.title: Kubernetes-based architecture announced for Cisco AI POD for Splunk
contextUpdates.text: Cisco’s announcement describes Kubernetes-based self-managed AI infrastructure for Splunk customers. It describes AI Assistant as available and Agent Launchpad as coming later in 2026.
contextUpdates.qualification: The statement is specific to self-managed AI and Cisco AI POD for Splunk. It does not establish an 11.x deployment model or confirm later delivery of the named planned feature.

aiAvailability.title: AI Availability
aiAvailability.boundary: Feature availability, edition entitlement, compatible versions, release stage and offering authorization are independent. A published capability or a supported hosting region does not establish that every tenant can enable it. Missing evidence remains explicit.
aiAvailability.regulatedQualification: Splunk's October 19, 2026 announcement claims FedRAMP High authorization for AI Assistant SPL authoring and explanation. Versioned SAIA installation guidance still describes limited IL2 support, excludes Agent Mode there and fixes runtime to Splunk-hosted models. Exact High app/version, mode, runtime and rollout remain unreconciled. This does not establish ES assistant, ITSI subagent, universal Moderate/High coverage or customer authorization.

capabilities.title: ES · AI Threat Graph Detection agent
capabilities.stage: Alpha feature · ES 8.8 release Controlled Availability
capabilities.description: Surface hidden malicious activity by stitching intermediate findings into evidence chains.
requirements: ES 8.8+ on Cloud; contact a Splunk representative to enable the alpha agent.
Turn on at least one risk-based detection; the guide says approximately one million events are needed to surface quality findings.
capabilities.runtime: ES Cloud agentic service; test mode routes generated findings to a detection test queue.
capabilities.qualification: Alpha status, ES 8.8 Controlled Availability, Premier entitlement, regional availability and offering/customer authorization are separate facts.
capabilities.condition: Confirm Premier entitlement, representative enablement, exact service region, risk-based detection coverage and adequate event volume.

capabilities.title: ES · AI SOC analyst agent
requirements: Premier, paired SOAR and representative enablement.
Cloud: Platform 10.2.x+, ES 8.6+ in the aggregate 8.8 table; the 8.7 task guide requires ES 8.7+.
CMP: Platform 10.4.x+, ES 8.8+, Cloud Connect 2.0.
The 8.7 task guide limits analysis to existing findings, the first 10 findings produced together and approximately 200 findings per tenant per day; only frontier models are supported.
capabilities.runtime: Agentic SOC services; the 8.7 task guide says the Splunk-hosted model option does not apply to this workflow. Paired SOAR has independent compatibility.
capabilities.qualification: The aggregate row is Premier. A separate 8.8 note assigns the Triage component to Essentials and the Response component to Premier, while the editions overview lists Triage under Premier; do not infer the whole workflow from a subcomponent. The 8.7 guide's connector/action inheritance and es_soar_integration_user_role requirement are task-specific authorization boundaries, not pairing evidence.
capabilities.condition: Confirm Premier access, exact Cloud or CMP prerequisites, paired SOAR compatibility, representative enablement, frontier-model support and inherited connector/asset permissions.

capabilities.title: Observability · AI Assistant
capabilities.description: Investigate, diagnose and understand system behavior with natural language across documented Observability product areas.
requirements: An Observability Cloud organization in a documented AWS (excluding GovCloud) or GCP realm.
Access to the underlying product data and permissions; log questions consume SVC quota.
capabilities.runtime: Splunk AI Assistant service subject to Azure OpenAI acceptable-use and content requirements.
capabilities.qualification: The page lists us3, but the current service description does not map that realm. Only the mapped realms are applied here. Chat access is limited to the most recent interaction within 30 days; essential-purpose data use applies and optional research sharing is off by default.
capabilities.condition: Confirm organization access, exact realm, permissions and data-use settings.

capabilities.title: Observability · AI troubleshooting agent
capabilities.version: July 8, 2026 service milestone · current feature guide
capabilities.description: Analyze potential root causes for supported APM and Kubernetes alerts and produce scoped remediation guidance.
requirements: An Observability Cloud organization in a non-Governmental realm.
Supported detectors and alerts using standard default metrics; custom metrics are not supported.
Users can run RCA manually; automatic organization enablement requires support.
capabilities.runtime: Splunk AI troubleshooting service integrated with the Assistant chat experience.
capabilities.qualification: AI remediation plans are currently limited to Kubernetes-related alerts. Availability does not establish entitlement, regional authorization or support for every detector.
capabilities.condition: Confirm organization opt-in, supported alert type, default-metric inputs and remediation scope.
